g.text: Tool-using LLM agents are increasingly deployed for information retrieval
tasks, combining language reasoning with external tools such as search and
databases (Qu et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2022).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Tool-using LLM agents are increasingly deployed for information retrieval tasks, combining language reasoning with external tools such as search and databases (Qu et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2022).

g.text: However, these agents exhibit systematic biases that degrade performance on
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) However, these agents exhibit systematic biases that degrade performance on ambiguous queries.

g.text: Anchoring bias—the tendency to over-rely on initially encountered
information—is particularly problematic: when presented with multiple
plausible candidates, agents disproportionately select the first-listed
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=2) Anchoring bias—the tendency to over-rely on initially encountered information—is particularly problematic: when presented with multiple plausible candidates, agents disproportionately select the first-listed option regardless of its correctness (Valencia-Clavijo, 2025; Yin et al., 2025).

g.text: Bias is costly in interactive settings
This bias is especially costly in interactive settings where agents must
clarify user intent before committing to an answer.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) This bias is especially costly in interactive settings where agents must clarify user intent before committing to an answer.

g.text: A natural hypothesis is that anchoring occurs because agents commit to
candidate interpretations before fully understanding user intent.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) A natural hypothesis is that anchoring occurs because agents commit to candidate interpretations before fully understanding user intent.

g.text: If the agent sees retrieval results early, the first candidate may anchor
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) If the agent sees retrieval results early, the first candidate may anchor subsequent reasoning and clarification questions.

g.text: The Intent Reconstruction Gate (IRG) intervention addresses this by forcing
clarification before retrieval exposure, potentially preventing premature
g.title: N7 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) The Intent Reconstruction Gate (IRG) intervention addresses this by forcing clarification before retrieval exposure, potentially preventing premature commitment to the first candidate.

g.text: This approach is motivated by cognitive science research showing that
anchoring effects can be mitigated through deliberation before anchor
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) This approach is motivated by cognitive science research showing that anchoring effects can be mitigated through deliberation before anchor exposure (Sumita et al., 2024).

g.text: We conduct controlled experiments to test the IRG hypothesis on
InteractComp-Anchor (Deng et al., 2025), a benchmark for ambiguous queries
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=1) We conduct controlled experiments to test the IRG hypothesis on InteractComp-Anchor (Deng et al., 2025), a benchmark for ambiguous queries requiring clarification.

g.text: We compare three conditions under identical interaction budgets: (A)
search-first baseline where the agent sees candidates before clarification,
(B) IRG clarify-first where clarification precedes retrieval, and (C)
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) We compare three conditions under identical interaction budgets: (A) search-first baseline where the agent sees candidates before clarification, (B) IRG clarify-first where clarification precedes retrieval, and (C) candidate-order control where the target is listed first.

g.text: (A) search-first baseline where the agent sees
g.title: N10a [Method: condition-A] (cites=0) (A) search-first baseline where the agent sees candidates before clarification
N10b [Method: condition-B] (cites=0) (B) IRG clarify-first where clarification precedes retrieval

g.text: (C) candidate-order control where the target is listed
g.title: N10c [Method: condition-C] (cites=0) (C) candidate-order control where the target is listed first

g.text: This design isolates the effect of clarification timing
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) This design isolates the effect of clarification timing from candidate presentation order.

g.text: Our results reveal a surprising negative finding: IRG does not work.
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) Our results reveal a surprising negative finding: IRG does not work.

g.text: The timing manipulation produces a negligible +0.95 percentage point
improvement over the search-first baseline (p = 0.42), while simply
reordering candidates to place the target first achieves a 13.33 percentage
g.title: N13 [Result] (cites=0) The timing manipulation produces a negligible +0.95 percentage point improvement over the search-first baseline (p = 0.42), while simply reordering candidates to place the target first achieves a 13.33 percentage point gain (p < 0.001).

g.text: The dominant factor in anchoring bias is candidate presentation order, not
g.title: N14 [Result] (cites=0) The dominant factor in anchoring bias is candidate presentation order, not clarification timing.

g.text: This suggests that for 7B-scale models, anchoring operates at the candidate
presentation stage rather than intent formation.
g.title: N15 [Result] (cites=0) This suggests that for 7B-scale models, anchoring operates at the candidate presentation stage rather than intent formation.

g.text: C1: first controlled test of timing
The first controlled test of whether clarification timing can
mitigate anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents, with
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) The first controlled test of whether clarification timing can mitigate anchoring bias in tool-using LLM agents, with pre-registered success criteria.

g.text: C2: order 14x more effective than IRG
Empirical evidence that candidate presentation order dominates
timing effects: reordering candidates is 14× more effective than
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) Empirical evidence that candidate presentation order dominates timing effects: reordering candidates is 14× more effective than the IRG intervention.

g.text: Actionable guidance for practitioners: focus on candidate
reordering) rather than clarification timing to mitigate anchoring
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) Actionable guidance for practitioners: focus on candidate presentation strategies (e.g., randomization, confidence-based reordering) rather than clarification timing to mitigate anchoring bias.
